\section[proponer]{proponer — to propose, to suggest}

\label{lesson:ES-C585-proponer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for positive, then the Spanish for negative.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: proponer}
\textbf{proponer} — \textquotedblleft{}to propose, to suggest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Propongo salir más temprano.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I propose leaving earlier.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{poner}: \emph{propongo, propuse, propuesto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{proponer} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{proponere} 'to put forward', \emph{pro} + \emph{ponere} 'to put', and rebuilt on \emph{poner} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proponer}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{proponer}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{proponer}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for positive, then the Spanish for negative, then say \emph{proponer} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does proponer mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To propose, to suggest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la propuesta]{la propuesta — the proposal}

\label{lesson:ES-C585-propuesta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for negative, then the Spanish for to propose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la propuesta}
\textbf{la propuesta} — \textquotedblleft{}the proposal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me gusta tu propuesta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I like your proposal.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Hacer una propuesta} — to make a proposal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{la propuesta} is built on \emph{propuesto}, the participle of \emph{proponer}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{proponere}, whose participle was \emph{propositus} 'put forward' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la propuesta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la propuesta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la propuesta}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for negative, then the Spanish for to propose, then say \emph{la propuesta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la propuesta mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The proposal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[advertir]{advertir — to warn; to notice}

\label{lesson:ES-C585-advertir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the proposal, then the Spanish for the suggestion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: advertir}
\textbf{advertir} — \textquotedblleft{}to warn; to notice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Te advierto que es difícil.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am warning you that it is difficult.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{sentir}: \emph{advierto, advirtió}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{advertir} is inherited from Latin \emph{advertere} 'to turn towards, to give attention', built from \emph{ad} and \emph{vertere} 'to turn' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
